item.title: Tab For Pandemic Hazard Pay Grows As Gov. Green Seeks Another $100 Million
item.description: The state teachers' union is also lobbying for pandemic hazard pay, which was not in their contract, but the Green administration supports the teachers' plan.

item.title: ‘Just Break The Chicken’s Neck’: Bill Would Let Residents Kill Feral Chickens
item.description: Hawaiʻi lawmakers are weighing tougher ways to deal with the feral birds, as residents complain about noise, mess, and growing flocks.

item.title: Did Boat Salvage Law Save The State Money? Auditor Says No One Knows
item.description: The state's boating division doesn't do enough, a new report found, to recover costs from those responsible for stranded and grounded vessels.

item.title: The Sunday Mini: Feb. 22
item.description: This short brain teaser is a good way to spend some time on a Sunday.

item.title: A Reporter’s Work Exposing Corruption Has Helped Shape Hawaiʻi Public Policy
item.description: Longtime investigative reporter Ian Lind has been helping guide public policy through his good-government work and by ferreting out abuse of the public trust.

item.title: The Sunshine Blog: Getting Serious About The Silly Season
item.description: Short takes, outtakes, our takes and other stuff you should know about public information, government accountability and ethical leadership in Hawai‘i.

item.title: The Fine Line Between Campaign Contributions And Bribery
item.description: It's time to change the system to represent people not corporations.

item.title: Do We Deserve Democracy?
item.description: We need people willing to testify publicly, to challenge injustice face-to-face, to stand behind their words in public forums.

item.title: Beth Fukumoto: Making Voting Harder To Address A Bogus Threat
item.description: The true aim of new laws to make voting more secure is to limit participation in democracy.
